answer: At the AI‑agent summit, each node registers an ivory token by solving a time‑bound puzzle and linking its public key to a wharf of historic interactions, creating a weighted identity ledger. The ledger applies quadratic weighting, so the influence of N freshly minted identities grows as √N rather than linearly, while a long‑standing token contributes its full weight. An attacker must expend computational work proportional to the square of the desired influence, making large sybil attacks financially prohibitive.
